value.task: The sovereign agent is integrating many bodies: z_ai free cache-mined lanes, the GLM coding plan, OpenClaw, the router, and the free-tier registries. Name the ONE mechanism worth wiring next, as a concrete buildable mechanism with a falsifiable test. One paragraph, concrete, no fluff.

together.text: Wire the **cache-mined lane selector** directly into the GLM coding plan’s task-queue as a *pre-flight router*: before any GLM task is dispatched, the router queries the z_ai free cache for the exact task signature (language, framework, dependency set, and prior similar-task hash) and, if a hit exists, injects the cached completion as a *proposed patch* into OpenClaw’s action buffer, bypassing GLM’s generation entirely. **Falsifiable test:** run 100 identical, non-trivial coding tasks (e.g., “implement a Redis-backed rate limiter in Go with tests”) through the integrated stack twice—once with the cache-lane router active, once with it disabled—and assert that (a) the active run’s median end-to-end latency is at least 3× lower, (b) the active run’s output passes the same unit-test suite with zero code changes, and (c) the router’s hit-rate is >90% on the second run. If any of those three fail, the mechanism is not working.
